name: walkthrough
title: Error handling from return codes to algebraic effects
description: A walk through the eleven labeled blocks of the tutorial. You watch return codes, exceptions, Option, Result, interpreter error types, and four strategies compared on the same task.

steps.description: The module copies the C return-code pattern. Each function returns a pair: a value and an errno code. A sentinel marks failure, with -1 for a file descriptor and None for data, and the constants ENOENT, EACCES and EINVAL name the error cases.

The caller checks err after every call. It prints the errno when a call fails and reads only when the open succeeded. The second half calls the functions and ignores both codes, so the bad descriptor flows on unnoticed.
At this step the caller calls c_style_open('myfile.txt', 'r') and unpacks the file descriptor and the errno code.

steps.question: The caller ignores the error codes on the second call. What does the program print for data2?

steps.description: Model 2 replaces return codes with exceptions. A function raises and the nearest matching except in the call stack handles it.
parse_int, read_config and process raise instead of returning codes. process calls read_config and parse_int with no try block, so any failure travels up to the caller.
The fourth case catches Exception, which is every failure other than a system exit. It swallows whatever went wrong, so a real bug looks like a handled case.
At this step process raises FileNotFoundError, and the nearest matching except FileNotFoundError catches it.

steps.question: The happy path writes 42 to a temp file and calls process on it. What does the program print for result?

steps.description: Model 3 makes absence explicit. A function returns Some(value) or Nothing instead of raising or returning None.

Some holds a value and Nothing holds none. Both define is_some, unwrap, map, and_then and unwrap_or, so a caller chains them without a type check. Option is the union of the two classes, and NOTHING is the shared Nothing instance.
pipeline parses a positive integer, converts it to a float, and divides. map runs only on a Some, and and_then runs the next function only when a value is present.

steps.question: pipeline('12', 0) parses 12 and then divides by zero. What does it return?

steps.description: Model 4 carries the reason for failure. A computation returns Ok(value) or Err(error), where error is a value you define.
Ok and Err mirror the Option methods with map, and_then, unwrap and unwrap_err. Each method leaves an Err untouched, so a chain stops at the first failure.
ParseError, MathError and IOError_ are the structured errors. Each one holds the fields that describe the failure, such as the input text or the filename.
The match statement reads the Result by shape. It binds the Ok value, then matches a ParseError or a MathError inside an Err and prints a different message for each.

steps.question: process parses the string and then takes its square root. What does process('9') return?

steps.description: Model 5 applies these ideas to an interpreter. Errors become an exception hierarchy that carries a source location.
SourceLocation holds a line and a column. InterpreterError holds a message and an optional location, and its __str__ appends the location when there is one.
UndefinedVariableError, TypeMismatchError and DivisionByZeroError subclass InterpreterError. Each one overrides __str__ to print its own kind of message.
eval_binop checks the operand types before it applies the operator. A bad type raises TypeMismatchError and a zero divisor raises DivisionByZeroError, each with the location it was given.

steps.question: The test cases run each expression through the evaluator. What does the program print for x / 0?

steps.description: Model 6 puts four strategies side by side on one task: find an element in a list, or report that it is missing.
find_sentinel returns the index or None. find_exception raises ValueError. find_tuple returns an index and a boolean, the Go style.
find_result returns a tagged pair, ('ok', index) or ('err', NotFoundError(target)). The error carries the missing target.
The loop searches for 30 and then for 99 and prints all four results each time. The contrast shows how each strategy reports the miss.

steps.question: The second search looks for 99, which is not in the list. What does the sentinel strategy print?
steps.answer: sentinel:  None  (caller must check for None)

steps.description: Exercise 1 builds a safe decorator that turns any function into one that returns a Result.
Ok and Err hold a value and an error. and_then runs the next function only on an Ok, and map transforms the value inside an Ok.
safe wraps a function in a try block. It returns Ok(result) on success and Err(str(e)) when the function raises.

steps.question: The loop runs sqrt(int(s)) for three strings. What does the program print for '-4'?

steps.description: Exercise 2 builds a stack trace for the interpreter. A list records the function names as calls enter and leave.

call_stack is the list of active names. InterpreterError joins the reversed stack into a trace. enter_function pushes a name, exit_function pops it, and raise_error attaches a copy of the stack to the error.
main calls foo, foo calls bar, and bar calls baz. Each function wraps its call in try/finally, so exit_function pops the name even when the error travels up.
At this step baz calls raise_error, which raises InterpreterError with the current call stack.
Exercise 3 compares Python's Optional[int] hint with the Option dataclass.
Some and Nothing define map and unwrap_or. Option is their union.
double_optional takes Optional[int] and returns None for None. double_option takes an Option and maps the doubling over it.

steps.question: The hint says Optional[int], but the caller passes the string 'hi'. What does the program print for double_optional('hi')?

steps.description: Exercise 4 collects every error in an expression instead of stopping at the first one.
EvalError holds the expression text and a message, and prints them as a labelled line.

eval_expr returns a value and a list of errors. It splits on the first operator, evaluates both sides, and extends the list with the errors from each side. A missing value or a zero divisor returns early with the errors collected so far.

steps.question: The environment defines x and y but not z. What error does the program report for x + z?

steps.description: Exercise 5 designs a full error hierarchy for an interpreter and pretty-prints each error.
SourceLocation holds the line, the column and the source text, and its __str__ points at the column with a caret. InterpreterError holds a message, a location and a suggestion.
LexError, ParseError, UndefinedVar and TypeError_ subclass InterpreterError. Each one overrides the category property, so pretty prints the right label.
pretty assembles the category and message, then the location, then the hint. It joins the parts with newlines.

steps.question: The list includes a ParseError for a missing close paren. What hint does it print?
